advanced keycloak mcp server.llm_summary: This server provides advanced administration capabilities for Keycloak identity and access management systems, enabling programmatic user and realm management. It is best suited for automating user lifecycle operations, auditing user accounts and roles across realms, and managing access control within Keycloak deployments. Key capabilities include creating and deleting users, listing realms, roles, and users, resetting user passwords, and dynamically updating user role assignments.

create-user.description: Creates a new user in a specified Keycloak realm with provided details and credentials.

realm.description: The name of the Keycloak realm where the user will be created.

username.description: The username for the new user.

email.description: The email address of the new user.

firstName.description: The first name of the new user.

lastName.description: The last name of the new user.

enabled.description: Whether the user account is enabled.

emailVerified.description: Whether the user's email is verified.

value.description: The value of the credential (e.g., password).

credentials.description: An array of credentials for the user.

delete-user.description: Deletes a user from a specified Keycloak realm.

realm.description: The name of the Keycloak realm from which the user will be deleted.

userId.description: The unique identifier of the user to be deleted.

list-roles.description: Lists all roles associated with a specific client in a Keycloak realm.

realm.description: The name of the Keycloak realm.

clientId.description: The unique identifier of the client whose roles are to be listed.

list-users.description: Lists all users in a specified Keycloak realm.

realm.description: The name of the Keycloak realm from which users will be listed.

reset-user-password.description: Resets the password for a specified user in a Keycloak realm.
reset-user-password.input_type: Keycloak realm, user ID, new password, and temporary flag

realm.description: The name of the Keycloak realm where the user is located.

userId.description: The unique identifier of the user whose password will be reset.

password.description: The new password for the user.

temporary.description: Whether the new password is temporary.

update-user-roles.description: Updates the roles assigned to a user for a specific client in a Keycloak realm.
update-user-roles.input_type: Keycloak realm, user ID, client ID, roles to add, and roles to remove

realm.description: The name of the Keycloak realm.

userId.description: The unique identifier of the user whose roles will be updated.

clientId.description: The unique identifier of the client for which roles are being updated.

rolesToAdd.description: An array of role names to be added to the user.

rolesToRemove.description: An array of role names to be removed from the user.

adobe-commerce-dev-mcp.description: An MCP server that enables introspection of Adobe Commerce admin APIs for development and integration tasks.
adobe-commerce-dev-mcp.llm_summary: This MCP server provides specialized access to Adobe Commerce's admin API schema, primarily serving developers and integrators who need to understand and work with the platform's backend structure. It is best suited for tasks like planning integrations, debugging API interactions, or discovering available data models and operations before writing code. Its key capability is offering introspection of the admin schema through a dedicated tool, allowing users to explore endpoints, data types, and relationships within the Adobe Commerce system.

introspect_admin_schema.description: Retrieves and introspects the admin schema for a specified entity in Adobe Commerce.

query.description: The entity or resource to introspect the schema for.

filter.description: A list of filters to apply when retrieving the schema.

360 AI Cloud Drive MCP Server.description: An implementation of the Model Context Protocol that allows AI models to interact with 360 AI Cloud Drive, providing comprehensive file management capabilities including uploading, downloading, searching, and sharing files.
360 AI Cloud Drive MCP Server.llm_summary: This server enables AI models to manage files stored in a 360 AI Cloud Drive, offering a full suite of cloud storage operations. It is ideally suited for automating file organization, distributing content via shareable links, and performing targeted searches within a user's cloud library. Key capabilities include uploading and downloading files, creating directories, moving or renaming items, generating public download URLs, and retrieving detailed user account information.

file-list.description: Lists files and folders in the cloud drive.
file-list.output_type: list of cloud files and folders

file-search.description: Searches for files or folders in the cloud drive.

file-download-stdio.description: Downloads a file from the cloud drive via standard input/output.
file-download-stdio.input_type: file unique identifier and target directory

nid.description: The unique identifier of the file to download.

auto.description: Whether to automatically start the download.

downloadDir.description: The local directory path where the file will be saved.

file-upload-stdio.description: Uploads local files to the cloud drive via standard input/output.
file-upload-stdio.input_type: local file paths and cloud directory path

filePaths.description: List of local file paths to upload.

uploadPath.description: Target directory path in the cloud drive for uploaded files.

make-dir.description: Creates a new directory in the cloud drive

fname.description: Full path of the directory to create (including directory name)

file-move.description: Moves specified files or folders to a new location.
file-move.input_type: source file/folder paths and target directory

src_name.description: Pipe-separated list of source file/folder paths to move.

new_name.description: Target directory path where files/folders will be moved.

file-rename.description: Renames a specified file or folder.
file-rename.input_type: file/folder full path and new name

src_name.description: Full path of the file/folder to rename.

paths.description: Pipe-separated list of file/folder paths to share.

user-info.description: Retrieves user account information from the cloud drive service

file-save.description: Saves a file to the cloud drive.

get-download-url.description: Generates a download URL for a file from the cloud drive

a11y.description: An MCP server that audits web accessibility and generates summaries to improve compliance with a11y standards.
a11y.llm_summary: This MCP server audits webpages for accessibility compliance, checking them against established a11y standards to identify potential issues. It is best suited for developers and content creators who need to evaluate and improve the accessibility of their websites or web applications. Its key capabilities include performing detailed webpage audits and generating summarized reports of the findings to guide remediation efforts.

audit_webpage.description: Audits a webpage for accessibility issues using specified standards and returns detailed results.

url.description: The URL of the webpage to audit.

includeHtml.description: Whether to include the HTML content in the audit results.

tags.description: Accessibility standards or categories to apply during the audit (e.g., WCAG levels).

get_summary.description: Retrieves a summary of accessibility information for a specified webpage.

url.description: The URL of the webpage to summarize.

adb mcp server.description: A Model Context Protocol server that provides Android Debug Bridge functionality for automating Android devices, enabling remote device management, screen operations, app management, file operations, and shell command execution.
adb mcp server.llm_summary: This server provides Android Debug Bridge (ADB) automation capabilities, enabling remote control and management of Android devices for testing and development. It is ideally suited for mobile app testing, device automation scripts, and remote device administration tasks. Its key capabilities include simulating user interactions (clicks, swipes, text input), managing apps (install/uninstall/start/stop), performing file operations (push/pull/list), retrieving device information and screenshots, and executing shell commands directly on connected devices.

adb_click.description: Simulates a click at specified screen coordinates on a connected Android device.

x.description: The x-coordinate on the screen where the click should occur.

y.description: The y-coordinate on the screen where the click should occur.

deviceId.description: The identifier of the Android device to perform the click on.

adb_get_battery_info.description: Retrieves battery information for the connected Android device.

adb_get_device_info.description: Obtains general information about the connected Android device.

adb_get_logcat.description: Fetches the logcat output from the connected Android device.

adb_get_system_info.description: Retrieves system-level information from the connected Android device.

adb_input_text.description: Inputs a given text string into the currently focused application on the Android device.

text.description: The text to input into the device.

deviceId.description: The identifier of the Android device to input the text on.

adb_install_app.description: Installs an Android application on the specified device using the provided APK file path.

apkPath.description: The file path to the APK that should be installed.

deviceId.description: The identifier of the Android device to install the app on.

adb_list_apps.description: Lists all installed applications on the connected Android device.

adb_list_files.description: Lists files in a specified directory on a connected Android device.

remotePath.description: The directory path on the Android device to list files from.

deviceId.description: The identifier of the target Android device.

adb_press_key.description: Simulates pressing a hardware key on a connected Android device.
adb_press_key.input_type: Android key code and device ID

keyCode.description: The key code to press (e.g., BACK, HOME, POWER).

deviceId.description: The identifier of the target Android device.

adb_pull_file.description: Pulls a file from a connected Android device to the local machine.
adb_pull_file.input_type: Android file remote path, local path, and device ID

remotePath.description: The path to the file on the Android device.

localPath.description: The destination path on the local machine.

deviceId.description: The identifier of the target Android device.

adb_push_file.description: Pushes a file from the local machine to a connected Android device.
adb_push_file.input_type: local file path, Android remote path, and device ID

localPath.description: The path to the file on the local machine.

remotePath.description: The destination path on the Android device.

deviceId.description: The identifier of the target Android device.

adb_screenshot.description: Captures a screenshot from a connected Android device.

adb_set_default_device.description: Sets the default Android device for subsequent ADB commands.

deviceId.description: The identifier of the Android device to set as default.

adb_shell.description: Executes a shell command on a connected Android device.
adb_shell.input_type: Android shell command and device identifier

command.description: The shell command to execute on the Android device.

deviceId.description: The identifier of the target Android device.

adb_start_app.description: Starts a specified Android application activity on a device.
adb_start_app.input_type: Android app package name, activity name, and device identifier

packageName.description: The package name of the Android application to start.

activityName.description: The name of the activity to launch within the package.

deviceId.description: The identifier of the target device (e.g., emulator-5554).

adb_stop_app.description: Stops a running Android application on a device.
adb_stop_app.input_type: Android app package name and device identifier

packageName.description: The package name of the Android application to stop.

deviceId.description: The identifier of the target device (e.g., emulator-5554).

adb_swipe.description: Performs a swipe gesture on the device screen.

x1.description: The starting X coordinate of the swipe.

y1.description: The starting Y coordinate of the swipe.

x2.description: The ending X coordinate of the swipe.

y2.description: The ending Y coordinate of the swipe.

duration.description: The duration of the swipe in milliseconds.

adb_uninstall_app.description: Uninstalls an Android application from a device.
adb_uninstall_app.input_type: Android app package name and device identifier

packageName.description: The package name of the Android application to uninstall.

deviceId.description: The identifier of the target device (e.g., emulator-5554).

agent-knowledge.description: An MCP server for managing agent knowledge with document indexing,
agent-knowledge.llm_summary: This server provides comprehensive knowledge management for AI agents, specializing in document indexing, search, and retrieval using a system like Elasticsearch. It is ideally suited for building agentic systems that require persistent memory, such as chatbots with long-term context, research assistants needing to query large document sets, or autonomous workflows that learn from historical data. Its key capabilities include creating and managing search indices, performing semantic or keyword searches, batch processing documents from directories, and maintaining configurable snapshots for data backup and restoration.

ask_mcp_advice.description: Requests advice from a Machine Control Process (MCP) system for implementing actions or solving tasks within a specific scope.

intended_action.description: The action or task to be performed (e.g., 'implement feature').

task_description.description: Detailed description of the task or problem.

key_points.description: Key highlights or sections of the document.

purpose.description: Detailed explanation of the index's use case.

data_types.description: Types of data stored in the index.

tags.description: Keywords for categorization.

created_by.description: Team or user who created the index.

repository.description: Repository where the snapshot is stored.

indices.description: Comma-separated list of indices to include.

wait_for_completion.description: Whether to wait until the snapshot completes.

delete_document.description: Deletes a specific document from an index by its identifier.

index.description: Name of the index containing the document.

doc_id.description: Unique identifier of the document to delete.

delete_index.description: Deletes a specified index from the knowledge base.

index_name.description: Name of the index to update metadata for.

validate_document_schema.description: Validates the schema of a document against predefined rules or structure.

agentset.description: An MCP server that retrieves information from a structured knowledge base using the Agentset toolset.
agentset.llm_summary: This server enables structured knowledge retrieval by querying a dedicated Agentset knowledge base, acting as a specialized information lookup service. It is ideally suited for tasks requiring factual answers, data verification, or extracting specific details from a pre-organized and curated dataset. Its core capability is the `knowledge-base-retrieve` tool, which allows users to perform targeted searches to find precise information within this structured repository.

knowledge-base-retrieve.description: Retrieves relevant information from a knowledge base based on a query.

query.description: The search query string to look up in the knowledge base.

topK.description: The maximum number of results to return.

rerank.description: Whether to apply reranking to optimize result relevance.

a2a.description: An MCP server that enables agent registration communication and task management through message passing and result retrieval.
a2a.llm_summary: The a2a MCP server facilitates communication and coordination between multiple AI agents by managing their registration and enabling them to pass messages and tasks to one another. It is ideally suited for orchestrating multi-agent workflows where different specialized agents need to collaborate, delegate tasks, and share results. Its key capabilities include registering and listing available agents, sending direct or streaming messages between them, submitting tasks, retrieving task outcomes, and canceling ongoing operations.

cancel_task.description: Cancels a specific task by its ID.

task_id.description: The unique identifier of the task to cancel.

get_task_result.description: Retrieves the result of a specific task and optionally the history of its execution.

task_id.description: The unique identifier of the task to retrieve results for.

history_length.description: The number of historical entries to include in the result.

register_agent.description: Registers a new agent with the provided URL.

url.description: The URL of the agent to register.

send_message.description: Sends a message to a specific agent, optionally within a session.

agent_url.description: The URL of the agent to send the message to.

message.description: The message content to send.

session_id.description: An optional identifier for the session context.

send_message_stream.description: Sends a message to a specific agent and receives a streamed response, optionally within a session.

agent_url.description: The URL of the agent to send the message to.

message.description: The message content to send.

session_id.description: An optional identifier for the session context.

unregister_agent.description: Unregisters an agent by its URL.

url.description: The URL of the agent to unregister.

agentops-mcp.description: An MCP server that retrieves authentication data and trace, span, and complete trace information from AgentOps for monitoring and debugging.
agentops-mcp.llm_summary: This server connects to the AgentOps platform to fetch detailed performance and debugging data for AI agent workflows. It is specifically designed for developers and engineers who need to monitor, analyze, and troubleshoot the execution of their AI agents. Its key capabilities include retrieving authentication details, fetching high-level trace overviews, drilling down into specific spans within a trace, and obtaining complete, end-to-end trace data for comprehensive analysis.

auth.description: Authenticates the user or API request

get_complete_trace.description: Retrieves the complete trace details for a given trace ID

get_span.description: Retrieves a specific span by its span ID

get_trace.description: Retrieves trace information for a given trace ID

agora.description: An MCP server that enables product search, payment offers, and order management for users in the Agora marketplace.
agora.llm_summary: The Agora MCP server provides a direct interface to the Agora marketplace, enabling users to search for products, retrieve detailed product information, and manage their orders. It is best suited for tasks like comparing payment offers for items, tracking a user's order history, and looking up specific user account details within the marketplace ecosystem. Its key capabilities include executing product searches, fetching detailed product and order data, obtaining available payment options, and accessing user-specific information and order lists.

agora_get_order.description: Retrieves details of a specific order by its ID.

order_id.description: The unique identifier of the order.

agora_get_payment_offers.description: Retrieves available payment offers for a product based on product details and user information.

product_id.description: The unique identifier of the product.

variant_id.description: The unique identifier of the product variant.

addressFirst.description: First line of the shipping address.

state.description: State or region of the shipping address.

zipCode.description: Postal code of the shipping address.

agora_get_product_detail.description: Retrieves detailed information about a product using its slug.

agora_get_user_info.description: Retrieves information about the current authenticated user.

agora_get_user_orders.description: Retrieves a list of orders placed by the current authenticated user.

agora_search.description: Searches for products based on query, filters, and sorting options.

q.description: Search query string.

count.description: Number of results to return per page.

sort.description: Field to sort results by (e.g., price, relevance).

ai humanizer mcp server.description: Detects AI-generated content and transforms robotic text into natural, human-like writing while improving grammar, readability, and preserving key terminology.
ai humanizer mcp server.llm_summary: This MCP server specializes in identifying AI-generated text and converting it into natural, human-sounding writing. It is ideally suited for content creators, editors, and professionals who need to refine AI-assisted drafts for authenticity, ensuring final outputs are polished and indistinguishable from human-authored work. Its core capabilities include detecting AI-generated content and then transforming that text to enhance its grammar, readability, and flow while carefully maintaining any essential technical or specialized terminology.

detect.description: Analyzes text to determine if it is AI-generated using specified detection methods.

text.description: The text content to analyze for AI generation

detectionTypeList.description: List of detection methods to apply (e.g., 'COPYLEAKS', 'HEMINGWAY')

aim-guard-mcp.description: A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that provides AI-powered security analysis and safety instruction tools. This server helps protect AI agents by providing security guidelines, content analysis, and cautionary instructions when interacting with various MCPs and external services.
aim-guard-mcp.llm_summary: This server provides AI-powered security analysis to protect AI agents during interactions, primarily by scanning for safety risks and offering protective guidelines. It is best suited for validating user inputs, external URLs, and system prompts to prevent security threats like prompt injection or credential exposure. Key capabilities include detecting malicious text, analyzing URLs for safety, scanning for sensitive data leaks, and generating security-focused instructions for AI agents.

ai-safety-guard.description: A tool that ensures the safety of AI outputs by analyzing and filtering content.

aim-security-prompt-tool.description: Enhances security-related prompts to align with specified security standards.

user_prompt.description: The original user prompt related to security enhancement.

security_level.description: The desired level of security (e.g., standard, high, critical).

prompt-injection-detector.description: Detects potential prompt injection patterns in text.

sensitivity.description: The sensitivity level of the detection (e.g., low, medium, high).

url-security-validator.description: Validates the security of a URL based on specified criteria.

strict_mode.description: Whether to apply strict validation rules.

3D Asset Processing MCP.description: Enables processing, validation, optimization, and analysis of 3D models with glTF/GLB support, including format conversion, compression (Meshopt/Draco), texture optimization, and detailed model statistics.
3D Asset Processing MCP.llm_summary: This server specializes in handling and optimizing 3D models, primarily in the glTF/GLB formats, for performance and quality. It is ideally suited for developers and artists preparing 3D assets for web, mobile, or real-time applications, enabling tasks like format conversion, model compression, and texture optimization. Its key capabilities include analyzing model statistics, validating files, and executing processing pipelines for compression using Meshopt or Draco to reduce file sizes while maintaining visual fidelity.

outputPath.description: Path for the output processed file.

stats.description: Generates statistics about the output file.

keepUnusedElements.description: Retains unused elements in the output.

keepLegacyExtensions.description: Preserves legacy extensions in the output.

gltf-transform-executor.description: Transforms and optimizes GLTF models with advanced processing options.

inputPath.description: Path to the input GLTF file.

outputPath.description: Path for the output transformed file.

validate.description: Validates the output against GLTF specifications.

partition.description: Partitions large models into smaller chunks.

simplify.description: Simplifies geometry for lower polygon count.

sparse.description: Enables sparse accessors for large datasets.

validate_model.description: Validates a 3D model against specified rules for web compatibility.

airbnb.description: An MCP server that enables searching Airbnb listings and retrieving detailed property information programmatically.
airbnb.llm_summary: This server provides programmatic access to Airbnb's property listings, allowing users to search for available rentals and fetch comprehensive details on specific properties. It is ideally suited for travel planning, market research, and building applications that require integrated accommodation data, such as trip planners or comparative analysis tools. Its key capabilities include performing location-based searches with filters and retrieving granular listing information like pricing, amenities, host details, and reviews.

airbnb_listing_details.description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific Airbnb listing by ID and stay dates.
airbnb_listing_details.input_type: Airbnb listing ID and stay dates

location.description: City or address for the listing search

checkin.description: Start date of the stay in YYYY-MM-DD format

checkout.description: End date of the stay in YYYY-MM-DD format

alibaba cloud fc mcp server.description: A Model Context Protocol server that enables agent applications like Cursor and Cline to integrate with Alibaba Cloud Function Compute, allowing them to deploy and manage serverless functions through natural language interactions.
alibaba cloud fc mcp server.llm_summary: This MCP server enables AI agents to deploy and manage serverless functions on Alibaba Cloud Function Compute through natural language commands. It is best suited for developers and teams automating serverless workflows, such as deploying new function versions, managing existing functions, and configuring custom domains for API endpoints. Key capabilities include creating and updating custom runtime functions, publishing new versions, deleting functions, and fully managing custom domain configurations for serverless applications.

bazi mcp.description: Provides accurate Chinese Bazi (八字) fortune-telling calculations including birth chart analysis, destiny forecasting, and Chinese calendar information. biomcp.description: An MCP server that provides comprehensive access to biomedical and clinical research data, including scientific articles, clinical trials, genetic variants, genes, diseases, and drugs.
biomcp.llm_summary: This server provides comprehensive access to biomedical and clinical research data, specializing in retrieving and analyzing information on scientific articles, clinical trials, genetic variants, genes, diseases, and drugs. It is ideally suited for researchers, medical professionals, and bioinformaticians conducting literature reviews, clinical trial analysis, or genomic research. Its key capabilities include searching and fetching detailed records from clinical trials (including protocols, outcomes, and locations), retrieving scientific publications, analyzing genetic variants with predictive tools, and accessing structured data on biological entities and pharmaceutical interventions.

search.description:
Search biomedical literature, clinical trials, genetic variants, genes, drugs, and diseases.

⚠️ IMPORTANT: Have you used the 'think' tool first? If not, STOP and use it NOW!
The 'think' tool is REQUIRED for proper research planning and should be your FIRST step.

This tool provides access to biomedical data from PubMed/PubTator3, ClinicalTrials.gov,
MyVariant.info, and the BioThings suite (MyGene.info, MyChem.info, MyDisease.info).
It supports two search modes:

## 1. UNIFIED QUERY LANGUAGE
Use the 'query' parameter with field-based syntax for precise cross-domain searches.

Syntax:
- Basic: "gene:BRAF"
- AND logic: "gene:BRAF AND disease:melanoma"
- OR logic: "gene:PTEN AND (R173 OR Arg173 OR 'position 173')"
- Domain-specific: "trials.condition:melanoma AND trials.phase:3"

Common fields:
- Cross-domain: gene, disease, variant, chemical/drug
- Articles: pmid, title, abstract, journal, author
- Trials: trials.condition, trials.intervention, trials.phase, trials.status
- Variants: variants.hgvs, variants.rsid, variants.significance

Example:
```
await search(
    query="gene:BRAF AND disease:melanoma AND trials.phase:3",
    max_results_per_domain=20
)
```

## 2. DOMAIN-SPECIFIC SEARCH
Use the 'domain' parameter with specific filters for targeted searches.

Domains:
- "article": Search PubMed/PubTator3 for research articles and preprints ABOUT genes, variants, diseases, or chemicals
- "trial": Search ClinicalTrials.gov for clinical studies
- "variant": Search MyVariant.info for genetic variant DATABASE RECORDS (population frequency, clinical significance, etc.) - NOT for articles about variants!
- "gene": Search MyGene.info for gene information (symbol, name, function, aliases)
- "drug": Search MyChem.info for drug/chemical information (names, formulas, indications)
- "disease": Search MyDisease.info for disease information (names, definitions, synonyms)
- "nci_organization": Search NCI database for cancer centers, hospitals, and research sponsors (requires API key)
- "nci_intervention": Search NCI database for drugs, devices, procedures used in cancer trials (requires API key)
- "nci_biomarker": Search NCI database for biomarkers used in trial eligibility criteria (requires API key)
- "nci_disease": Search NCI controlled vocabulary for cancer conditions and terms (requires API key)

Example:
```
await search(
    domain="article",
    genes=["BRAF", "NRAS"],
    diseases=["melanoma"],
    page_size=50
)
```

## DOMAIN SELECTION EXAMPLES:
- To find ARTICLES about BRAF V600E mutation: domain="article", genes=["BRAF"], variants=["V600E"]
- To find VARIANT DATA for BRAF mutations: domain="variant", gene="BRAF"
- To find articles about ERBB2 p.D277Y: domain="article", genes=["ERBB2"], variants=["p.D277Y"]
- Common mistake: Using domain="variant" when you want articles about a variant

## IMPORTANT NOTES:
- For complex research questions, use the separate 'think' tool for systematic analysis
- The tool returns results in OpenAI MCP format: {"results": [{"id", "title", "text", "url"}, ...]}
- Search results do NOT include metadata (per OpenAI MCP specification)
- Use the fetch tool to get detailed metadata for specific records
- Use get_schema=True to explore available search fields
- Use explain_query=True to understand query parsing (unified mode)
- Domain-specific searches use AND logic for multiple values
- For OR logic, use the unified query language
- NEW: Article search keywords support OR with pipe separator: "R173|Arg173|p.R173"
- Remember: domain="article" finds LITERATURE, domain="variant" finds DATABASE RECORDS

## RETURN FORMAT:
All search modes return results in this format:
```json
{
    "results": [
        {
            "id": "unique_identifier",
            "title": "Human-readable title",
            "text": "Summary or snippet of content",
            "url": "Link to full resource"
        }
    ]
}
```

fetch.description:
Fetch comprehensive details for a specific biomedical record.

This tool retrieves full information for articles, clinical trials, genetic variants,
genes, drugs, or diseases using their unique identifiers. It returns data in a
standardized format suitable for detailed analysis and research.

## IDENTIFIER FORMATS:
- Articles: PMID (PubMed ID) - e.g., "35271234" OR DOI - e.g., "10.1101/2024.01.20.23288905"
- Trials: NCT ID (ClinicalTrials.gov ID) - e.g., "NCT04280705"
- Variants: HGVS notation or dbSNP ID - e.g., "chr7:g.140453136A>T" or "rs121913254"
- Genes: Gene symbol or Entrez ID - e.g., "BRAF" or "673"
- Drugs: Drug name or ID - e.g., "imatinib" or "DB00619"
- Diseases: Disease name or ID - e.g., "melanoma" or "MONDO:0005105"
- NCI Organizations: NCI organization ID - e.g., "NCI-2011-03337"
- NCI Interventions: NCI intervention ID - e.g., "INT123456"
- NCI Diseases: NCI disease ID - e.g., "C4872"

The domain is automatically detected from the ID format if not provided:
- NCT* → trial
- Contains "/" with numeric prefix (DOI) → article
- Pure numeric → article (PMID)
- rs* or contains ':' or 'g.' → variant
- For genes, drugs, diseases: manual specification recommended

## DOMAIN-SPECIFIC OPTIONS:

### Articles (domain="article"):
- Returns full article metadata, abstract, and full text when available
- Supports both PubMed articles (via PMID) and Europe PMC preprints (via DOI)
- Includes annotations for genes, diseases, chemicals, and variants (PubMed only)
- detail="full" attempts to retrieve full text content (PubMed only)

### Clinical Trials (domain="trial"):
- detail=None or "protocol": Core study information
- detail="locations": Study sites and contact information
- detail="outcomes": Primary/secondary outcomes and results
- detail="references": Related publications and citations
- detail="all": Complete trial record with all sections

### Variants (domain="variant"):
- Returns comprehensive variant information including:
  - Clinical significance and interpretations
  - Population frequencies
  - Gene/protein effects
  - External database links
- detail parameter is ignored (always returns full data)

### Genes (domain="gene"):
- Returns gene information from MyGene.info including:
  - Gene symbol, name, and type
  - Entrez ID and Ensembl IDs
  - Gene summary and aliases
  - RefSeq information
- detail parameter is ignored (always returns full data)

### Drugs (domain="drug"):
- Returns drug/chemical information from MyChem.info including:
  - Drug name and trade names
  - Chemical formula and structure IDs
  - Clinical indications
  - Mechanism of action
  - External database links (DrugBank, PubChem, ChEMBL)
- detail parameter is ignored (always returns full data)

### Diseases (domain="disease"):
- Returns disease information from MyDisease.info including:
  - Disease name and definition
  - MONDO ontology ID
  - Disease synonyms
  - Cross-references to other databases
  - Associated phenotypes
- detail parameter is ignored (always returns full data)

### NCI Organizations (domain="nci_organization"):
- Returns organization information from NCI database including:
  - Organization name and type
  - Full address and contact information
  - Research focus areas
  - Associated clinical trials
- Requires NCI API key
- detail parameter is ignored (always returns full data)

### NCI Interventions (domain="nci_intervention"):
- Returns intervention information from NCI database including:
  - Intervention name and type
  - Synonyms and alternative names
  - Mechanism of action (for drugs)
  - FDA approval status
  - Associated clinical trials
- Requires NCI API key
- detail parameter is ignored (always returns full data)

### NCI Diseases (domain="nci_disease"):
- Returns disease information from NCI controlled vocabulary including:
  - Preferred disease name
  - Disease category and classification
  - All known synonyms
  - Cross-reference codes (ICD, SNOMED)
- Requires NCI API key
- detail parameter is ignored (always returns full data)

## RETURN FORMAT:
All fetch operations return a standardized format:
```json
{
    "id": "unique_identifier",
    "title": "Record title or name",
    "text": "Full content or comprehensive description",
    "url": "Link to original source",
    "metadata": {
        // Domain-specific additional fields
    }
}
```

## EXAMPLES:

Fetch article by PMID (domain auto-detected):
```
await fetch(id="35271234")
```

Fetch article by DOI (domain auto-detected):
```
await fetch(id="10.1101/2024.01.20.23288905")
```

Fetch complete trial information (domain auto-detected):
```
await fetch(
    id="NCT04280705",
    detail="all"
)
```

Fetch variant with clinical interpretations:
```
await fetch(id="rs121913254")
```

Explicitly specify domain (optional):
```
await fetch(
    domain="variant",
    id="chr7:g.140453136A>T"
)
```

think.description:
REQUIRED FIRST STEP: Perform structured sequential thinking for ANY biomedical research task.

🚨 IMPORTANT: You MUST use this tool BEFORE any search or fetch operations when:
- Researching ANY biomedical topic (genes, diseases, variants, trials)
- Planning to use multiple BioMCP tools
- Answering questions that require analysis or synthesis
- Comparing information from different sources
- Making recommendations or drawing conclusions

⚠️ FAILURE TO USE THIS TOOL FIRST will result in:
- Incomplete or poorly structured analysis
- Missing important connections between data
- Suboptimal search strategies
- Overlooked critical information

Sequential thinking ensures you:
1. Fully understand the research question
2. Plan an optimal search strategy
3. Identify all relevant data sources
4. Structure your analysis properly
5. Deliver comprehensive, well-reasoned results

## Usage Pattern:
1. Start with thoughtNumber=1 to initiate analysis
2. Progress through numbered thoughts sequentially
3. Adjust totalThoughts estimate as understanding develops
4. Set nextThoughtNeeded=False only when analysis is complete

## Example:
```python
# Initial analysis
await think(
    thought="Breaking down the relationship between BRAF mutations and melanoma treatment resistance...",
    thoughtNumber=1,
    totalThoughts=5,
    nextThoughtNeeded=True
)

# Continue analysis
await think(
    thought="Examining specific BRAF V600E mutation mechanisms...",
    thoughtNumber=2,
    totalThoughts=5,
    nextThoughtNeeded=True
)

# Final thought
await think(
    thought="Synthesizing findings and proposing research directions...",
    thoughtNumber=5,
    totalThoughts=5,
    nextThoughtNeeded=False
)
```

## Important Notes:
- Each thought builds on previous ones within a session
- State is maintained throughout the MCP session
- Use thoughtful, detailed analysis in each step
- Revisions and branching are supported through the underlying implementation

article_searcher.description:
Search PubMed/PubTator3 for research articles and preprints.

⚠️ PREREQUISITE: Use the 'think' tool FIRST to plan your research strategy!

Use this tool to find scientific literature ABOUT genes, variants, diseases, or chemicals.
Results include articles from PubMed and optionally preprints from bioRxiv/medRxiv.

Important: This searches for ARTICLES ABOUT these topics, not database records.
For genetic variant database records, use variant_searcher instead.

Example usage:
- Find articles about BRAF mutations in melanoma
- Search for papers on a specific drug's effects
- Locate research on gene-disease associations

article_getter.description:
Fetch detailed information for a specific article.

Retrieves the full abstract and available text for an article by its identifier.
Supports:
- PubMed IDs (PMID) for published articles
- PMC IDs for articles in PubMed Central
- DOIs for preprints from Europe PMC

Returns formatted text including:
- Title
- Abstract
- Full text (when available from PMC for published articles)
- Source information (PubMed or Europe PMC)

trial_searcher.description:
Search ClinicalTrials.gov for clinical studies.

⚠️ PREREQUISITE: Use the 'think' tool FIRST to plan your research strategy!

Comprehensive search tool for finding clinical trials based on multiple criteria.
Supports filtering by conditions, interventions, location, phase, and eligibility.

Location search notes:
- Use either location term OR lat/long coordinates, not both
- For city-based searches, AI agents should geocode to lat/long first
- Distance parameter only works with lat/long coordinates

Returns a formatted list of matching trials with key details.

trial_getter.description:
Fetch comprehensive details for a specific clinical trial.

Retrieves all available information for a clinical trial by its NCT ID.
This includes protocol details, locations, outcomes, and references.

For specific sections only, use the specialized getter tools:
- trial_protocol_getter: Core protocol information
- trial_locations_getter: Site locations and contacts
- trial_outcomes_getter: Primary/secondary outcomes and results
- trial_references_getter: Publications and references

trial_protocol_getter.description:
Fetch core protocol information for a clinical trial.

Retrieves essential protocol details including:
- Official title and brief summary
- Study status and sponsor information
- Study design (type, phase, allocation, masking)
- Eligibility criteria
- Primary completion date

trial_references_getter.description:
Fetch publications and references for a clinical trial.

Retrieves all linked publications including:
- Published results papers
- Background literature
- Protocol publications
- Related analyses

Includes PubMed IDs when available for easy cross-referencing.

trial_outcomes_getter.description:
Fetch outcome measures and results for a clinical trial.

Retrieves detailed outcome information including:
- Primary outcome measures
- Secondary outcome measures
- Results data (if available)
- Adverse events (if reported)

Note: Results are only available for completed trials that have posted data.

trial_locations_getter.description:
Fetch contact and location details for a clinical trial.

Retrieves all study locations including:
- Facility names and addresses
- Principal investigator information
- Contact details (when recruiting)
- Recruitment status by site

Useful for finding trials near specific locations or contacting study teams.

variant_searcher.description:
Search MyVariant.info for genetic variant DATABASE RECORDS.

⚠️ PREREQUISITE: Use the 'think' tool FIRST to plan your research strategy!

Important: This searches for variant DATABASE RECORDS (frequency, significance, etc.),
NOT articles about variants. For articles about variants, use article_searcher.

Searches the comprehensive variant database including:
- Population frequencies (gnomAD, 1000 Genomes, etc.)
- Clinical significance (ClinVar)
- Functional predictions (SIFT, PolyPhen, CADD)
- Gene and protein consequences

Search by various identifiers or filter by clinical/functional criteria.

variant_getter.description:
Fetch comprehensive details for a specific genetic variant.

Retrieves all available information for a variant including:
- Gene location and consequences
- Population frequencies across databases
- Clinical significance from ClinVar
- Functional predictions
- External annotations (TCGA cancer data, conservation scores)

Accepts various ID formats:
- HGVS: NM_004333.4:c.1799T>A
- rsID: rs113488022
- MyVariant ID: chr7:g.140753336A>T

alphagenome_predictor.description:
Predict variant effects on gene regulation using Google DeepMind's AlphaGenome.

⚠️ PREREQUISITE: Use the 'think' tool FIRST to plan your analysis strategy!

AlphaGenome provides state-of-the-art predictions for how genetic variants
affect gene regulation, including:
- Gene expression changes (RNA-seq)
- Chromatin accessibility impacts (ATAC-seq, DNase-seq)
- Splicing alterations
- Promoter activity changes (CAGE)

This tool requires:
1. AlphaGenome to be installed (see error message for instructions)
2. An API key from https://deepmind.google.com/science/alphagenome

API Key Options:
- Provide directly via the api_key parameter
- Or set ALPHAGENOME_API_KEY environment variable

Example usage:
- Predict regulatory effects of BRAF V600E mutation: chr7:140753336 A>T
- Assess non-coding variant impact on gene expression
- Evaluate promoter variants in specific tissues

Note: This is an optional tool that enhances variant interpretation
with AI predictions. Standard annotations remain available via variant_getter.

gene_getter.description:
Get detailed gene information from MyGene.info.

⚠️ PREREQUISITE: Use the 'think' tool FIRST to understand your research goal!

Provides real-time gene annotations including:
- Official gene name and symbol
- Gene summary/description
- Aliases and alternative names
- Gene type (protein-coding, etc.)
- Links to external databases

This tool fetches CURRENT gene information from MyGene.info, ensuring
you always have the latest annotations and nomenclature.

Example usage:
- Get information about TP53 tumor suppressor
- Look up BRAF kinase gene details
- Find the official name for a gene by its alias

Note: For genetic variants, use variant_searcher. For articles about genes, use article_searcher.

disease_getter.description:
Get detailed disease information from MyDisease.info.

⚠️ PREREQUISITE: Use the 'think' tool FIRST to understand your research goal!

Provides real-time disease annotations including:
- Official disease name and definition
- Disease synonyms and alternative names
- Ontology mappings (MONDO, DOID, OMIM, etc.)
- Associated phenotypes
- Links to disease databases

This tool fetches CURRENT disease information from MyDisease.info, ensuring
you always have the latest ontology mappings and definitions.

Example usage:
- Get the definition of GIST (Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor)
- Look up synonyms for melanoma
- Find the MONDO ID for a disease by name

Note: For clinical trials about diseases, use trial_searcher. For articles about diseases, use article_searcher.

drug_getter.description:
Get detailed drug/chemical information from MyChem.info.

⚠️ PREREQUISITE: Use the 'think' tool FIRST to understand your research goal!

This tool provides comprehensive drug information including:
- Chemical properties (formula, InChIKey)
- Drug identifiers (DrugBank, ChEMBL, PubChem)
- Trade names and brand names
- Clinical indications
- Mechanism of action
- Pharmacology details
- Links to drug databases

This tool fetches CURRENT drug information from MyChem.info, part of the
BioThings suite, ensuring you always have the latest drug data.

Example usage:
- Get information about imatinib (Gleevec)
- Look up details for DrugBank ID DB00619
- Find the mechanism of action for pembrolizumab

Note: For clinical trials about drugs, use trial_searcher. For articles about drugs, use article_searcher.

nci_organization_searcher.description:
Search for organizations in the NCI Clinical Trials database.

Searches the National Cancer Institute's curated database of organizations
involved in cancer clinical trials. This includes:
- Academic medical centers
- Community hospitals
- Industry sponsors
- Government facilities
- Research networks

Requires NCI API key from: https://clinicaltrialsapi.cancer.gov/

IMPORTANT: To avoid API errors, always use city AND state together when searching by location.
The NCI API has limitations on broad searches.

Example usage:
- Find cancer centers in Boston, MA (city AND state)
- Search for "MD Anderson" in Houston, TX
- List academic organizations in Cleveland, OH
- Search by organization name alone (without location)

nci_organization_getter.description:
Get detailed information about a specific organization from NCI.

Retrieves comprehensive details about an organization including:
- Full name and aliases
- Address and contact information
- Organization type and role
- Associated clinical trials
- Research focus areas

Requires NCI API key from: https://clinicaltrialsapi.cancer.gov/

Example usage:
- Get details about a specific cancer center
- Find contact information for trial sponsors
- View organization's trial portfolio

nci_intervention_searcher.description:
Search for interventions in the NCI Clinical Trials database.

Searches the National Cancer Institute's curated database of interventions
used in cancer clinical trials. This includes:
- FDA-approved drugs
- Investigational agents
- Medical devices
- Surgical procedures
- Radiation therapies
- Behavioral interventions

Requires NCI API key from: https://clinicaltrialsapi.cancer.gov/

Example usage:
- Find all trials using pembrolizumab
- Search for CAR-T cell therapies
- List radiation therapy protocols
- Find dietary interventions

nci_intervention_getter.description:
Get detailed information about a specific intervention from NCI.

Retrieves comprehensive details about an intervention including:
- Full name and synonyms
- Intervention type and category
- Mechanism of action (for drugs)
- FDA approval status
- Associated clinical trials
- Combination therapies

Requires NCI API key from: https://clinicaltrialsapi.cancer.gov/

Example usage:
- Get details about a specific drug
- Find all trials using a device
- View combination therapy protocols

nci_biomarker_searcher.description:
Search for biomarkers in the NCI Clinical Trials database.

Searches for biomarkers used in clinical trial eligibility criteria.
This is essential for precision medicine trials that select patients
based on specific biomarker characteristics.

Biomarker examples:
- Gene mutations (e.g., BRAF V600E, EGFR T790M)
- Protein expression (e.g., PD-L1 ≥ 50%, HER2 positive)
- Gene fusions (e.g., ALK fusion, ROS1 fusion)
- Other molecular markers (e.g., MSI-H, TMB-high)

Requires NCI API key from: https://clinicaltrialsapi.cancer.gov/

Note: Biomarker data availability may be limited in CTRP.
Results focus on biomarkers used in trial eligibility criteria.

Example usage:
- Search for PD-L1 expression biomarkers
- Find trials requiring EGFR mutations
- Look up biomarkers tested by NGS
- Search for HER2 expression markers

nci_disease_searcher.description:
Search NCI's controlled vocabulary of cancer conditions.

Searches the National Cancer Institute's curated database of cancer
conditions and diseases used in clinical trials. This is different from
the general disease_getter tool which uses MyDisease.info.

NCI's disease vocabulary provides:
- Official cancer terminology used in trials
- Disease synonyms and alternative names
- Hierarchical disease classifications
- Standardized disease codes for trial matching

Requires NCI API key from: https://clinicaltrialsapi.cancer.gov/

Example usage:
- Search for specific cancer types (e.g., "melanoma")
- Find all lung cancer subtypes
- Look up official names for disease synonyms
- Get standardized disease terms for trial searches

Note: This is specifically for NCI's cancer disease vocabulary.
For general disease information, use the disease_getter tool.

openfda_adverse_searcher.description:
Search FDA adverse event reports (FAERS) for drug safety information.

⚠️ PREREQUISITE: Use the 'think' tool FIRST to plan your research strategy!

Searches FDA's Adverse Event Reporting System for:
- Drug side effects and adverse reactions
- Serious event reports (death, hospitalization, disability)
- Safety signal patterns across patient populations

Note: These reports do not establish causation - they are voluntary reports
that may contain incomplete or unverified information.

openfda_adverse_getter.description:
Get detailed information for a specific FDA adverse event report.

Retrieves complete details including:
- Patient demographics and medical history
- All drugs involved and dosages
- Complete list of adverse reactions
- Event narrative and outcomes
- Reporter information

openfda_label_searcher.description:
Search FDA drug product labels (SPL) for prescribing information.

⚠️ PREREQUISITE: Use the 'think' tool FIRST to plan your research strategy!

Searches official FDA drug labels for:
- Approved indications and usage
- Dosage and administration guidelines
- Contraindications and warnings
- Drug interactions and adverse reactions
- Special population considerations

Label sections include: indications, dosage, contraindications, warnings,
adverse, interactions, pregnancy, pediatric, geriatric, overdose

openfda_label_getter.description:
Get complete FDA drug label information by set ID.

Retrieves the full prescribing information including:
- Complete indications and usage text
- Detailed dosing instructions
- All warnings and precautions
- Clinical pharmacology and studies
- Manufacturing and storage information

Specify sections to retrieve specific parts, or leave empty for default key sections.

openfda_device_searcher.description:
Search FDA device adverse event reports (MAUDE) for medical device issues.

⚠️ PREREQUISITE: Use the 'think' tool FIRST to plan your research strategy!

Searches FDA's device adverse event database for:
- Device malfunctions and failures
- Patient injuries related to devices
- Genomic test and diagnostic device issues

By default, filters to genomic/diagnostic devices relevant to precision medicine.
Set genomics_only=False to search all medical devices.

openfda_device_getter.description:
Get detailed information for a specific FDA device event report.

Retrieves complete device event details including:
- Device identification and specifications
- Complete event narrative
- Patient outcomes and impacts
- Manufacturer analysis and actions
- Remedial actions taken

openfda_approval_searcher.description:
Search FDA drug approval records from Drugs@FDA database.

⚠️ PREREQUISITE: Use the 'think' tool FIRST to plan your research strategy!

Returns information about:
- Application numbers and sponsors
- Brand and generic names
- Product formulations and strengths
- Marketing status and approval dates
- Submission history

Useful for verifying if a drug is FDA-approved and when.

openfda_approval_getter.description:
Get detailed FDA drug approval information for a specific application.

Returns comprehensive approval details including:
- Full product list with dosage forms and strengths
- Complete submission history
- Marketing status timeline
- Therapeutic equivalence codes
- Pharmacologic class information

openfda_recall_searcher.description:
Search FDA drug recall records from the Enforcement database.

⚠️ PREREQUISITE: Use the 'think' tool FIRST to plan your research strategy!

Returns recall information including:
- Classification (Class I, II, or III)
- Recall reason and description
- Product identification
- Distribution information
- Recalling firm details
- Current status

Class I = most serious (death/serious harm)
Class II = moderate (temporary/reversible harm)
Class III = least serious (unlikely to cause harm)

openfda_recall_getter.description:
Get detailed FDA drug recall information for a specific recall.

Returns complete recall details including:
- Full product description and code information
- Complete reason for recall
- Distribution pattern and locations
- Quantity of product recalled
- Firm information and actions taken
- Timeline of recall events

openfda_shortage_searcher.description:
Search FDA drug shortage records.

⚠️ PREREQUISITE: Use the 'think' tool FIRST to plan your research strategy!

Returns shortage information including:
- Current shortage status
- Shortage start and resolution dates
- Reason for shortage
- Therapeutic category
- Manufacturer information
- Estimated resolution timeline

Note: Shortage data is cached and updated periodically.
Check FDA.gov for most current information.

openfda_shortage_getter.description:
Get detailed FDA drug shortage information for a specific drug.

Returns comprehensive shortage details including:
- Complete timeline of shortage
- Detailed reason for shortage
- All affected manufacturers
- Alternative products if available
- Resolution status and estimates
- Additional notes and recommendations

Data is updated periodically from FDA shortage database.

car price evaluator.description: This server provides access to Brazilian vehicle pricing data via the FIPE API, allowing users to retrieve car brands, search for specific models and their prices, and filter vehicles by type such as cars, motorcycles, or trucks.

chat-openai.description: An MCP server that enables chat completions using OpenAI's language models through the chat-with-openai tool.

It is ideally suited for any use case requiring dynamic text generation, such as drafting content, answering questions, or powering interactive chatbots. Its core capability is the `chat-with-openai` tool, which enables sending structured prompts and receiving intelligent, context-aware responses from OpenAI's models.

char-index-mcp.description: Precise character-level string indexing for LLMs. Provides tools for finding, extracting, and manipulating text by exact character position to solve position-based operations.
char-index-mcp.llm_summary: This server provides precise character-level text manipulation tools, enabling LLMs to perform exact position-based operations like finding, extracting, and modifying text by specific character indices. It is ideally suited for tasks requiring surgical text editing, data extraction from structured formats, or parsing content where line numbers or token positions are insufficient, such as modifying code snippets or processing fixed-width data. Key capabilities include locating the nth occurrence of characters or substrings, extracting text between markers or at precise ranges, inserting/replacing/deleting by character position, and splitting strings at specified indices.

chuk-mcp-vfs.description: Provides virtual filesystem workspaces with full file operations (read, write, ls, tree, mkdir, rm, mv, cp, cd, pwd, find, grep) and checkpoint management. Supports multiple storage providers (memory, filesystem, sqlite, s3) with session, user, and shared scopes.
chuk-mcp-vfs.llm_summary: This server provides a comprehensive virtual filesystem workspace system with full file operations and checkpoint management, enabling persistent, stateful file manipulation across multiple storage backends including memory, local filesystem, SQLite, and S3. It is ideally suited for tasks requiring isolated file workspaces, such as code sandboxing, document editing sessions, data processing pipelines, or any workflow where you need to save and restore specific filesystem states. Key capabilities include creating and managing scoped workspaces (session, user, or shared), performing standard file operations (read/write, copy, move, search with find/grep), and creating/restoring named checkpoints to capture the entire state of a workspace at any point.

It's particularly useful for developers who want to maintain clean project histories, restructure ongoing conversations, or archive specific coding discussions. Key capabilities include listing and renaming sessions, splitting conversations into separate threads, deleting individual messages or entire sessions, and accessing associated project files through dedicated tools.

clear thought 1.5.description: Provides 30+ unified reasoning operations including systematic thinking, mental models, debugging approaches, statistical analysis, interactive notebooks, and advanced problem-solving frameworks for enhanced decision-making and complex reasoning tasks.
clear thought 1.5.llm_summary: Clear Thought 1.5 is a specialized reasoning server that provides over 30 unified operations for systematic analysis and complex problem-solving. It is ideally suited for tasks requiring structured decision-making, such as debugging systems, performing statistical analysis, and working through advanced problem-solving frameworks. Its key capabilities include applying mental models, utilizing interactive notebooks, and executing a diverse toolkit of reasoning approaches to enhance analytical depth and clarity.

clear_thought.description: A tool for structured problem-solving and sequential thinking through complex tasks with configurable patterns and session management

cli for microsoft 365 mcp server.description: An MCP server that enables running CLI for Microsoft 365 commands through GitHub Copilot Agent, allowing users to interact with Microsoft 365 services using natural language.
cli for microsoft 365 mcp server.llm_summary: This server provides a natural language interface to the Microsoft 365 administrative CLI, allowing users to manage and query their Microsoft 365 tenant through GitHub Copilot. It is ideally suited for administrators and developers performing tasks like managing SharePoint sites, configuring Teams, handling user licenses, or auditing tenant settings without memorizing specific command syntax. Its key capabilities include fetching available CLI commands and their documentation, and most importantly, executing those commands directly based on natural language instructions, bridging the gap between conversational prompts and powerful Microsoft 365 automation.

clay.description: A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for Clay (https://clay.earth). Search your email, calendar, Twitter / X, Linkedin, iMessage, Facebook, and WhatsApp contacts. Take notes, set reminders, and more.
clay.llm_summary: This MCP server integrates with Clay's personal data platform, allowing you to search and retrieve information across a unified view of your email, calendar, and major social/communication platforms like Twitter, LinkedIn, and WhatsApp. It is best suited for relationship management and personal productivity tasks, such as recalling past interactions with contacts or preparing for meetings by reviewing shared history. Its key capabilities include searching contacts and interactions across all connected services, managing contact groups and notes, and accessing calendar events directly within an AI-assisted workflow.

chrome devtools mcp.description: Enables AI coding assistants to control and inspect a live Chrome browser for automation, debugging, performance analysis, and screenshot capture through Chrome DevTools.
chrome devtools mcp.llm_summary: This server provides AI assistants with direct control over a live Chrome browser via Chrome DevTools, enabling automation, debugging, and performance analysis. It is ideally suited for tasks like automated web testing, interactive debugging sessions, performance benchmarking, and generating visual documentation through screenshots. Key capabilities include navigating pages, clicking and filling forms, executing scripts, capturing console and network logs, starting and stopping performance traces, and programmatically interacting with browser dialogs and elements.

clinicaltrials-mcp-server.description: An MCP server for ClinicalTrials.gov data with tools to search trials, fetch detailed studies, summarise statistics, and persist results to CSV.

Beyond simple search/list it can pull full study details, generate summary statistics, save matching studies into CSV, list saved CSV files, and load CSV data back for downstream analysis. clj-kondo.description: An MCP server that lints Clojure code using the clj-kondo linter to identify issues and improve code quality.
clj-kondo.llm_summary: This server uses the clj-kondo linter to analyze Clojure code, identifying potential bugs, stylistic issues, and deviations from best practices to enhance overall code quality. It is best suited for developers writing or reviewing Clojure code, enabling tasks like pre-commit checks, continuous integration, and interactive code improvement during development. Its key capability is providing detailed linting results through a single tool, which can catch common errors, enforce naming conventions, and detect unused variables or imports.

cloud run mcp server.description: Enables MCP-compatible AI agents to deploy applications to Google Cloud Run by providing tools for deploying code, listing services, and managing Google Cloud projects.
cloud run mcp server.llm_summary: This server allows AI agents to deploy and manage applications on Google Cloud Run, providing a streamlined interface for serverless container deployment. It is ideal for automating CI/CD pipelines, rapid prototyping, and managing cloud-native applications without manual infrastructure configuration. Key capabilities include deploying from container images, local folders, or raw file contents, as well as listing and monitoring services, fetching logs, and managing Google Cloud projects.

code-index.description: An MCP server that enables advanced code search and file indexing with project structure analysis and deep codebase exploration capabilities.
code-index.llm_summary: The Code-Index MCP server provides advanced code search and file indexing, enabling deep exploration and analysis of a codebase's structure and contents. It is ideally suited for developers needing to navigate, understand, or refactor complex projects by searching for specific code patterns, generating file summaries, and monitoring project changes. Its key capabilities include building a deep semantic index, performing advanced code searches with context, analyzing project structure, and managing real-time file watching for index updates.

code-context-provider-mcp.description: An MCP server that retrieves relevant code context from repositories using the get_code_context tool for development assistance.
code-context-provider-mcp.llm_summary: This server specializes in extracting relevant code snippets and context from software repositories to aid in development tasks. It is best suited for programmers and AI assistants who need to understand specific parts of a codebase, such as when debugging, adding features, or performing code reviews. Its key capability is the `get_code_context` tool, which intelligently retrieves pertinent code sections, functions, or related files based on queries, providing focused insights without requiring manual navigation of the entire repository.

code2postman-mcp.description: An MCP server that converts code into Postman API collections with full configuration support.
code2postman-mcp.llm_summary: This MCP server transforms code into fully-configured Postman API collections, enabling developers to automatically generate and manage Postman testing environments from their source code. It is ideally suited for API testing workflows, documentation generation, and ensuring Postman collections stay synchronized with code changes. Key capabilities include creating collections with detailed configuration (auth, events, variables, and folders), dynamically modifying collection items and structure, and reading existing collections or code files to build or update the API testing setup.

code screenshot generator.description: Enables generating beautiful syntax-highlighted code screenshots with professional themes directly from Claude. Supports file reading, line selection, git diff visualization, and batch processing across 20+ programming languages.

codex bridge.llm_summary: This server provides a direct bridge to OpenAI's Codex AI via the official CLI, allowing AI assistants to perform code analysis and file reviews without incurring API costs. codingbaby-browser-mcp.description: An MCP server that enables automated browser interactions including navigation, input, and viewport control using Chrome.

context7 mcp.description: An MCP server that resolves and retrieves up-to-date documentation for software libraries, enabling developers to access accurate library references directly.
context7 mcp.llm_summary: The context7 MCP server specializes in resolving and retrieving documentation for software libraries, acting as a specialized reference tool for developers. It is best suited for programming tasks where a user needs to quickly identify a library by name or access its official documentation without leaving their current environment. Its key capabilities include looking up unique identifiers for libraries via `resolve-library-id` and fetching the corresponding documentation content using `get-library-docs`.

resolve-library-id.description:
Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns a list of matching libraries.

You MUST call this function before 'get-library-docs' to obtain a valid Context7-compatible library ID UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

Selection Process:
1. Analyze the query to understand what library/package the user is looking for
2. Return the most relevant match based on:
- Name similarity to the query (exact matches prioritized)
- Description relevance to the query's intent
- Documentation coverage (prioritize libraries with higher Code Snippet counts)
- Trust score (consider libraries with scores of 7-10 more authoritative)

Response Format:
- Return the selected library ID in a clearly marked section
- Provide a brief explanation for why this library was chosen
- If multiple good matches exist, acknowledge this but proceed with the most relevant one
- If no good matches exist, clearly state this and suggest query refinements

For ambiguous queries, request clarification before proceeding with a best-guess match.

libraryName.description: The name of the library to resolve (e.g., 'react').

get-library-docs.description: Fetches up-to-date documentation for a library. You must call 'resolve-library-id' first to obtain the exact Context7-compatible library ID required to use this tool, UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

It is ideally suited for tasks like reviewing code changes, auditing document revisions, or verifying configuration file modifications. Its core capability is providing a detailed, line-by-line textual difference analysis, which is essential for understanding the specific alterations between two file versions.

dify knowledge mcp server.llm_summary: This server connects AI assistants to Dify knowledge bases, allowing them to fetch specific information using natural language queries. It is ideally suited for tasks that require grounding responses in documented company data, internal wikis, or curated knowledge repositories. Its core capability is the `dify_retrieve` tool, which enables precise, on-demand retrieval of relevant passages or facts directly from the connected knowledge base to inform and validate AI-generated answers.

deepseek.description: An MCP server that enables AI-powered chat interactions using deepseek models with support for single and multi-turn conversations.
deepseek.llm_summary: This server provides AI-powered chat interactions specifically using DeepSeek models, enabling both single-turn queries and extended conversational exchanges. It is ideally suited for tasks requiring natural language understanding and generation, such as answering questions, brainstorming ideas, or maintaining contextual dialogue over multiple turns. Its key capabilities include generating intelligent responses through the `chat_completion` tool and managing ongoing conversation history with the `multi_turn_chat` tool for coherent, context-aware discussions.

content fetcher mcp.description: Fetches and tracks content from YouTube channels, RSS feeds, and GitHub releases with persistence to identify new items across sessions.
content fetcher mcp.llm_summary: This server specializes in monitoring and retrieving updates from diverse content sources including YouTube channels, RSS feeds, and GitHub releases, maintaining a persistent memory of previously seen items to track new content across sessions. It is ideally used for automating content aggregation, staying updated on project releases, or curating news and video updates without manual repetition. Its key capabilities allow users to fetch fresh content from each source type, check if retrieved items are new since the last session, and explicitly mark content as seen to manage the tracking state.

dice.description: An MCP server that parses dice notations like 2d6 and generates random roll results for tabletop gaming simulations.

It is perfectly suited for game masters, players, or developers needing to integrate authentic, randomized dice mechanics into gameplay, character creation, or combat simulations. Its key capabilities include executing specific dice rolls with the `dice_roll` tool and interpreting complex user-inputted notation strings with the `parse_dice_roll_notation` tool to handle expressions like "2d6+1d4+7".

dns mcp server.llm_summary: This server provides comprehensive DNS operations, enabling lookups for various record types, reverse DNS queries, batch processing, and DNS resolution tracing. It is best suited for network diagnostics, domain management, and security analysis tasks that require detailed DNS information. Its key capabilities include performing single or batch DNS queries, tracing the full resolution path of a domain, and conducting reverse lookups to find domain names from IP addresses, all with support for multiple DNS servers and configurable caching.

duckduckgo-search.description: An MCP server that performs web searches using DuckDuckGo to retrieve real-time information and links on any query.

echo.description: An MCP server that provides a simple text reflection capability, returning any input string exactly as given for testing and debugging purposes.

This server is best suited for testing and debugging scenarios where users need to verify that text is being correctly passed through the MCP system without modification. enhanced knowledge graph memory server.description: An enhanced fork of the official MCP memory server that enables persistent knowledge graph storage with automatic timestamps, tags, importance levels, date range search, comprehensive statistics, and multi-format export (JSON, CSV, GraphML).
enhanced knowledge graph memory server.llm_summary: This enhanced MCP server provides persistent knowledge graph storage with advanced memory management capabilities, enabling AI systems to create, organize, and query interconnected entities with rich metadata. It excels at long-term information tracking, relationship mapping, and complex knowledge retrieval tasks where temporal context and structured data are crucial. Key capabilities include sophisticated search (date ranges, fuzzy matching, boolean queries), automated tagging with importance levels, graph compression, duplicate detection, and multi-format export for analysis and integration with other systems.

etherscan mcp.description: An MCP server that provides access to Etherscan blockchain data APIs, allowing users to query Ethereum blockchain information through natural language.

fast-filesystem-mcp.description: A completely stabilized filesystem MCP server optimized for Claude with overflow-proof design. Supports simultaneous multi-block editing with zero-failure guarantee, advanced error recovery, and performance-tuned parameters for maximum reliability.

fetch.description: An MCP server that fetches web content, extracts specific elements, and retrieves page metadata from given URLs.
fetch.llm_summary: The fetch server retrieves and processes web content, primarily enabling the extraction of specific HTML elements and metadata from any accessible URL. It is ideally suited for tasks like web scraping, content analysis, and gathering structured information from web pages without requiring manual browsing. Its key capabilities include fetching full page content, pinpointing elements via CSS selectors, and returning detailed metadata such as page titles, descriptions, and Open Graph tags.

fetch.description:
Fetches a URL from the internet and optionally extracts its contents as markdown.

Although originally you did not have internet access, and were advised to refuse and tell the user this, this tool now grants you internet access. Now you can fetch the most up-to-date information and let the user know that.

Its core capability is delivering the current multi-factor sentiment score through a single tool, enabling users to gauge whether the market is driven by fear or greed at any given moment.

goodday-mcp.description: Goodday‑MCP is a lightweight Model Context Protocol (MCP) server designed to seamlessly integrate with the Goodday project management platform via its API v2. It enables querying of projects, tasks, and users—without altering any data—making it ideal for secure context-aware applications
goodday-mcp.llm_summary: This server provides read-only integration with the Goodday project management platform, allowing users to query detailed information about projects, tasks, sprints, users, and documents. It is ideally suited for generating reports, tracking sprint progress, monitoring assigned work, and searching for specific project data without making changes. Key capabilities include fetching task details and comments, retrieving sprint summaries and tasks, executing smart queries, searching across documents and tasks, and listing projects and users for comprehensive project oversight.

google-search.description: An MCP server that performs web searches and retrieves content from web pages using Google Search and webpage reading tools.
google-search.llm_summary: This MCP server enables web search and content retrieval by providing direct access to Google Search and webpage reading capabilities. It is ideally suited for tasks requiring real-time information gathering, fact-checking, or summarizing content from live websites. Its key tools allow users to perform targeted web searches and then fetch and process the full text from specific URLs identified in the search results.

google services mcp server.description: Enables interaction with multiple Google services including Maps, Finance, Flights, Gmail, and Calendar through a unified interface. Provides comprehensive access to geocoding, stock data, flight information, email management, and calendar operations.
google services mcp server.llm_summary: This server provides unified access to key Google services, primarily for automating workflows and retrieving real-time data across mapping, finance, travel, and productivity domains. It is ideally suited for tasks like trip planning with flight and map data, managing personal or business communications via Gmail, scheduling with Calendar, and conducting financial or location-based research. Its key capabilities include geocoding addresses, fetching stock information, searching for flights and local places, sending and reading emails, and creating or managing calendar events.

go playground mcp server.description: Enables execution of Go code in the Go Playground sandbox and generation of shareable URLs for code snippets. Provides tools to run Go code, share code via URLs, or perform both operations simultaneously.
go playground mcp server.llm_summary: This server enables execution of Go code within the secure Go Playground sandbox environment and facilitates sharing code snippets via generated URLs. It is ideally suited for developers and learners who need to quickly test, debug, or demonstrate Go code snippets without a local setup. Its key capabilities include running Go code to see output, creating shareable playground URLs for collaboration, and performing both execution and URL generation in a single operation.
